questions.statement: Which is the first month of the year?
questions.context: In an English class in Medellín, the teacher points to a calendar of the year.

options.text: January.
options.feedback: January is the first month of the year.

options.text: March.
options.feedback: March is the third month, not the first.

options.text: June.
options.feedback: June is the sixth month, not the first.

options.text: December.
options.feedback: December is the twelfth and last month.

questions.explanation: Remembering the names and order of the months of the year in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: According to the text, when is the writer's birthday?
questions.context: Read: "My birthday is on May 3rd. My best friend's birthday is on August 15th."

options.text: On May 3rd.
options.feedback: The text says "My birthday is on May 3rd."

options.text: On August 15th.
options.feedback: That is the best friend's birthday, not the writer's.

options.text: On December 25th.
options.feedback: December 25th is not mentioned in the text.

options.text: On January 1st.
options.feedback: January 1st is not mentioned in the text.

questions.explanation: Understanding simple written information about dates and birthdays.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the ordinal number correctly?
questions.context: A student in Cali wants to say when her birthday is using an ordinal number.

options.text: My birthday is on the 12th of September.
options.feedback: "12th" is the correct ordinal form for twelve.

options.text: My birthday is on the 12 of September.
options.feedback: The ordinal needs "th": "12th".

options.text: My birthday is on September 12th of.
options.feedback: The word order is wrong; "of" must come before the month.

options.text: My birthday is in the 12nd of September.
options.feedback: "12nd" is not a correct ordinal form.

questions.explanation: Applying ordinal numbers (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th...) to express dates in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which holiday is celebrated in Colombia on July 20th?
questions.context: A poster in a school in Bogotá lists Colombian holidays in English.

options.text: Independence Day.
options.feedback: Colombia celebrates its Independence Day on July 20th.

options.text: Christmas Day.
options.feedback: Christmas is celebrated on December 25th.

options.text: New Year's Day.
options.feedback: New Year's Day is on January 1st.

options.text: Halloween.
options.feedback: Halloween is on October 31st and is not a Colombian national holiday.

questions.explanation: Recognizing Colombian holidays and their dates in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: A student wants to ask a new friend in English about his birthday.

options.text: When is your birthday?
options.feedback: "When is your birthday?" is the correct way to ask for the date.

options.text: When your birthday is?
options.feedback: The word order is incorrect; the verb "is" must come before the subject.

options.text: What birthday is yours?
options.feedback: This is not a correct question in English.

options.text: How many birthday you have?
options.feedback: This question does not ask for the date of a birthday.

questions.explanation: Forming polite questions in English to ask about birthdays and dates.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the main idea of the text?
questions.context: Read: "In Colombia, many families celebrate birthdays with a party, cake, and music. Children usually invite their friends and play games together."

options.text: Colombian birthday parties usually include cake, music, and games with friends.
options.feedback: The text describes how families celebrate birthdays in Colombia.

options.text: Birthdays in Colombia are never celebrated with friends.
options.feedback: The text says children usually invite their friends.

options.text: Only adults celebrate birthdays in Colombia.
options.feedback: The text mentions children celebrating and playing games.

options.text: Birthday parties are forbidden in Colombia.
options.feedback: The text describes celebrations, not prohibitions.

questions.explanation: Analyzing a short paragraph in English to identify its main idea.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Why do the two sentences use different prepositions?
questions.context: Read the sentences: "The party is in December." and "The party is on December 5th."

options.text: "In" is used with months and "on" with specific dates.
options.feedback: We say "in December" for the month and "on December 5th" for a date.

options.text: "On" is used with months and "in" with specific dates.
options.feedback: It is the opposite: "in" goes with months and "on" with dates.

options.text: Both prepositions can be exchanged without changing meaning.
options.feedback: The prepositions are not interchangeable here.

options.text: Months never take a preposition in English.
options.feedback: Months do take the preposition "in".

questions.explanation: Analyzing the correct use of the prepositions "in" and "on" with months and dates.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Based on the text, which statement is true?
questions.context: Read: 'Maria's birthday is on October 9th. Her school has a concert on October 7th and a football game on October 12th.'

options.text: Maria's birthday comes after the concert but before the football game.
options.feedback: October 9th is after October 7th and before October 12th.

options.text: Maria's birthday is before the concert.
options.feedback: October 9th is after the concert on October 7th.

options.text: Maria's birthday is after the football game.
options.feedback: October 9th is before the game on October 12th.

options.text: Maria's birthday is on the same day as the concert.
options.feedback: The birthday and the concert are on different days.

questions.explanation: Evaluating dates in sequence to determine the correct order of events in English.
questions.subject: ingles
